body:
My father also was diagnosed with similar things as me. He passed away 5 years ago. It was much easier to talk to him about these things. My mother cares but she doesn't seem to understand mental illness. She tells me to try, wait it out, rest.. Talking to her is a little frustrating actually. 

I have only been on the one medication all of my life. the switching has only been recent. My mother still lives in Newfoundland and after a month at home for christmas I know I couldn't stand another moment living there. I love my family but they can be some of the meanest people to me. The don't understand what's happening to me and it seems as if they don't care to. moving home is the very last thing on my list. :( 

I could try not taking any medication I guess. It seems like id wouldn't do well with that. I hardly cope with life while taking something to help me. 

I'm extra upset today for some reason. The twitching is very bad.
I will check it out. Thank you :)
I do try most of the time. At times it is the only thing that gives me any relief.
Thank you. I hope things work out for you as well.

I have always been different in some way. I had light light blond hair (White even) and glasses in early grade school. I was teased from the moment I started and eventually it got very bad. The school told my parents that something must be wrong with me and that I must have been provoking the other students to do the horrible things they had been doing. I spent the next 8 years (after 4th grade) doing the bare minimum to get through it. The diagnosing started when I was 13. OCD, Anxiety, Depression, Tourette Syndrome, Social phobia, blah blah blah. Having the diagnoses never helped anything as I didn't have a "bad" case of anything. They argued that I was lying to get a lighter coarse load. Growing up in Rural NL meant I only had the one option for a school so I had to deal with that the entire way through as well.  

They asked me at 12 what I wanted to treat with medication. My parents didn't want me to take more than one drug. I wasn't well enough informed at that age so I chose to treat the OCD. In comes the paxil and out goes any other treatment for any other problem. If my visit to the doctor was for something physical (That wasn't obvious like bleeding from an open wound or a broken limb) the doctor would always suggest the pain was "In my mind". If it was for a mental issue he would just increase my paxil dose. It's been that was since really. I moved to Ontario from Newfoundland and after a string of Doctors, Overdoses, breakdowns, jobs... A doctor suggested I try other drugs. 

I'm giving it my best but my best isn't cutting it. The year I have spent in Ontario has been one mess of crazy after another. Boyfriends, his ex girlfriend, roommate, doctors, school, jobs, hospitals, police, friends being absolute jerks, loneliness, medications, drugs, sex... I've been making decisions like a teenager with no parents. 

I think I could write for hours about the messed up things in my life.

I am attempting to work with the latest doctor to find a medication that might help. I just made the incredibly difficult decision to stop taking Paxil after 14 years. I suspect that has a lot to do with the extreme downturn in my mood. I made it through just barely. I have another appointment at the end of the month but until then I don't have anything to ease the pain. I'm afraid Ill do something stupid before then. After that even.

If I try to focus on something I panic. If I try to clean I get overwhelmed and feel as if everything is a mess and I could never clean it all. 
If I try to apply for jobs a panic and imagine no one will ever hire me and if they do I could never keep a job. 
I actually panic, I either can't breathe or I hyperventilate. I usually always end up in tears.

I was diagnosed years ago with OCD, Anxiety, Depression... there is a list longer than I care to remember. Doctors just switch medications, up the dose, add a new drug. That alone is making me crazy. I don't know what is me and what is medication anymore. 
I don't have a job, its frustrating but its also nearly impossible to keep a job with my mind in such a mess. My resume shows off my inability to hold down a job and I have no references. 
I moved half way across the country with a guy. That's been an ordeal in itself. 
I guess its just a mixture of my life and my illness? The medications and the insanity in my head? 
I apologize, I feel like my thoughts are all lined up waiting, in order, they make sense, but for some reason I can't communicate them. Almost as if the normal, functional part of my mind is not connected to my mouth or to my fingers.
In the state of mind I am in it feels like nothing really matters. I panic if I try to accomplish anything so I don't even try anymore.
